app.title: SeismicLens — Interactive Seismic Waveform Analyzer
app.summary: A person loads a single seismic trace: they generate a synthetic earthquake, upload a MiniSEED or CSV file, or fetch a waveform from an FDSN data centre by network, station, channel and time window. They set a zero-phase bandpass filter and an STA/LTA detector in the sidebar. Every view then recomputes: the filtered waveform with the picked P arrival, its amplitude, phase and power spectra with summary frequencies, a spectrogram, and the STA/LTA ratio with its trigger windows. They finish by downloading the filtered signal, spectrum, PSD and STA/LTA ratio as CSV files.

task.text: Filter a seismic trace, pick the P-wave onset automatically, describe the trace's frequency content, and export the processed series for further analysis.

data.text: One single-channel waveform sampled at a fixed rate, either synthetic or recorded, along with the frequency and time–frequency series computed from it and a fixed layered velocity table.
data.item: a seismogram trace from one station channel

stage.text: exploring and processing raw seismograms before further analysis

mechanism.text: The sidebar holds the data source, the filter and the detector settings. Every change re-runs the processing chain (taper, bandpass, FFT, PSD, STFT, STA/LTA), and the processed signal feeds a metric strip and the tabbed charts: waveform, spectra, spectrogram, STA/LTA and velocity model. Display toggles turn the raw overlay, phase, PSD, spectrogram and STA/LTA views on or off, and an export tab writes each computed series to CSV.

field.text: waveform processing and STA/LTA phase picking in seismology

workflow.name: process a single signal and export its derived series

steps.here: A radio picks one of four sources: a synthetic quake set by magnitude, depth, distance, noise and duration sliders; a MiniSEED upload; a one- or two-column CSV upload; or an FDSN fetch by provider, network, station, location, channel and UTC window.

Choose the low cut, high cut and order of a zero-phase Butterworth bandpass, which can be switched off to compare against the raw trace. Then set the STA window, the LTA window and the trigger threshold.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each change recomputes the sampling rate, duration, peak amplitude, dominant frequency, picked P arrival and S–P delay, which are shown as metric cards.

steps.step: locate where the event starts in the record
steps.here: The waveform chart marks the STA/LTA P pick (and the synthetic S arrival). The STA/LTA tab plots the ratio against the threshold, shades the trigger windows and reports the first trigger.

steps.step: look at the signal in the frequency domain
steps.here: Read the FFT amplitude spectrum, with optional phase spectrum and Welch PSD, plus the dominant frequency, spectral centroid and RMS bandwidth. Read the STFT spectrogram as a time–frequency heatmap.
Download buttons save the filtered signal, the FFT (frequency, amplitude, phase), the PSD (counts²/Hz and dB) and the STA/LTA ratio as CSV files, with a preview table of the first 200 samples.

distinctive: The onset is picked automatically: the arrival time is the first point where the short-term/long-term energy ratio crosses a set threshold.
The filter is zero-phase (forward-backward), so it removes noise without shifting arrival times.
Synthetic traces come from a layered crustal velocity model, so the S–P delay gives an epicentral distance by the Wadati method.
Waveforms can be pulled live from FDSN data centres by network, station, location, channel and time window.
